articles.title: Jane Fonda, Robert De Niro & Other Figures Sign Letter Backing Chris Van Hollen For Majority Leader — Amid A Chuck Schumer Aide's Prank

articles.content:
Jane Fonda , Robert De Niro and Chelsea Handler are among the entertainment figures who have signed on to a letter backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in his bid to become Senate majority leader over Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY).

The letter, signed by about three dozen figures describing themselves as donors, fundraisers and artists, stated that in this year's midterms, "voters delivered not on ly a mandate but an opportunity for change: a government that delivers real value in the daily lives of working families."

"That change will only come from renewed leadership with a vision for the future," the letter stated. "The Democratic Party has a trust and credibility problem, and fixing it requires Senate leaders willing to challenge the entrenched interests and power structures that protect those in power, in both parties." The election for majority leader, to be held early next month, has highlighted party divisions, including among donors and in the entertainment industry, and even after the whopping victories of Democrats across the country in the midterms.

Noting that the upcoming vote on a Senate leader will be chosen by secret ballot, the letter called on the caucus to support Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer, the current minority leader who had been the presumptive favorite to win following Democrats huge gains in which they flipped control of the chamber.

Others who signed on to the letter include Bruce Cohen, Padma Lakshmi, Laurie David, David Mandel, Fisher Stevens, Marisa Tomei, Amy Ziering and Morgan Spector.

In a statement. De Niro said, "Americans voted for the change necessary to fight the corruption, cruelty, and policies of Trump and his Epstein class cronies. That's why I'm supporting change in Senate leadership. Chris Van Hollen is a progressive leader and a fierce fighter. He's the right person to lead the Senate majority." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Van Hollen has pitched his candidacy as a necessary response to the midterm results and that Democrats' unexpected gains were also calls for change, coming from the left and the middle of the party.

"The voters responsible for the Blue Tsunami want fundamental change and bold, new ideas. Simply put, Chuck Schumer is the past and Chris Van Hollen is the present and the future," Cohen said.

Schumer has insisted that he will emerge victorious, and even some entertainment industry observers believe that he will return to the post.

Mathew Littman, who leads The Working Group, which organizes Hollywood creatives, said via email, "Senator Schumer just led one of the great political wins of all time. He earned two years to lead his fellow Senate Democrats."

A Times analysis last week showed that Schumer had the public support of 16 senators and Van Hollen had the backing of 6, with 4 more calling for change. But more than two dozen senators' backing is unknown.

Spokespersons for Schumer and Van Hollen did not return requests for comment.

But a campaign aide to Schumer, Angelo Roefaro, told Politico that he was behind a bit of pranks-manship in advance of the release of the letter. He gained access to the Google doc draft of the letter and added Frank Sinatra's name to the list of signatories, and subbed in Schumer's name for Van Hollen. A Times reporter initially posted a copy of the letter endorsing Van Hollen, but with Sinatra's name still included, before replacing it with an image of the corrected letter, per Politico. Roefaro told Politico that Schumer was unaware of the prank.

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. Confirms "Science Bro" Replacements in Avengers: Doomsday, And It's Perfect
articles.summary: Marvel Studios The first big interviews and media profiles on Avengers: Doomsday are starting to hit, as we enter the final countdown to the epic crossover film's release. One of the latest featured articles on Doomsday has star Robert Downey Jr. sharing some of the finer details about the film and how his return as Doctor Doom […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The first big interviews and media profiles on Avengers: Doomsday are starting to hit, as we enter the final countdown to the epic crossover film's release. One of the latest featured articles on Doomsday has star Robert Downey Jr. sharing some of the finer details about the film and how his return as Doctor Doom compares to starring in the previous Avengers movie as Tony Stark/Iron Man.

One of the most unexpected fan-favorite moments of the original Avengers (2012) movie was seeing Tony Stark and Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo) geeking out together over alien technology in a SHIELD science lab. Stark and Banner quickly became the Marvel Cinematic Universe's signature bromance, under the nickname "The Science Bros." The Science Bros went on to be the source of Ultron and The Vision's creation in Avengers: Age of Ultron ; by Avengers: Endgame, they cracked time travel, and both used the Infinity Gauntlet to save/restore the universe.

Obviously, the original Science Bros' time is now done, but Downey has revealed that the tradition will continue into a new era during Avengers: Doomsday .

In EW's new feature on Avengers: Doomsday , Downey reveals more about how the film will establish a new "Science Bros" team in Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) and Doom (Downey). “We are the guys that always pick up each other’s FaceTimes, because we literally have just become a new version of science bros,” Downey said.

The film will apparently tap into traditional Marvel lore, in which Reed Richards and Victor Von Doom meet as the two leading geniuses at their university. They establish a deep bond, which (in comic lore) inevitably gets strained after Victor's insatiable ambitions for power leave him horribly disfigured, and he retreats into the persona of being an iron-fisted ruler hid behind an iron mask. “The love and respect that Doom and Reed have for each other in Doomsday is critical to the storytelling,” director Joe Russo said.

Fantastic Four: First Steps star Pedro Pascal further breaks down the MCU history between Doom and Reed Richards, confirming that these new science bros are more like polar opposites rather than collaborators with common ground. “Reed struggled to use his power of intelligence and understanding of science for the good of his family and the good of mankind," Pascal explained. "Whereas Doom, with equal, if not superior, intellectual power, uses it for questionable attainment of power. There’s so much delicious conflict there, standing on other ends of the spectrum.”

This entire discussion about Reed Richards and Doom's dynamic in Avengers: Doomsday soft-confirms one of the bigger rumors about the story: Doom isn't some arch-nemesis or even an antagonist at the start of the film; he's working with Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four to save the multiverse – or at least, save a portion of it that is ruled by Doom.

The descriptions from Downey and Pascal clearly reveal how Doom and Reed will be working together to solve the collapse of the Marvel multiverse – that is, until Doom sees an opportunity to grab the ultimate power of creating a new world for himself. The final Avengers: Doomsday trailer featured more scenes that seem to depict the moment when heroes like Steve Rogers(?) and Thor confront Doom about his true intentions and force him to shift into full villain mode, while Reed looks on in bewilderment, finally having to confront his old friend himself, asking, "Victor, did you do this!?" in response to some nefarious thing Doom has done. That also explains Sue Storm's (Vanessa Kirby) voiceover narration in a previous trailer, about knowing Victor but being unaware of just how "broken" he was, and how drastically he would react to multiversal calamity.

As I've said before: this may be the riskiest move Avengers: Doomsday is making with its story. Having Doom pretend to be heroic won't fool anyone in the audience, so hopefully it creates a more complex and compelling story as we get to know more about Doom and his true motivations .

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th. Ready for the next era of Marvel Science Bros?

articles.title: Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and ’70s, Dies at 87
articles.summary: People like her “don’t go away at all,” photographer Franco Rubartelli said. “They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”
articles.content:
Veruschka, the chameleonic, long-limbed supermodel and performance artist who photographer Richard Avedon once pronounced “the most beautiful woman in the world,” has died. She was 87.

Veruschka died in her home in Berlin, the German newspaper Bild reported.

On Instagram, her former partner and photographer Franco Rubartelli acknowledged her death and noted “she wasn’t just a great model. She was an elegant woman, sensitive, brave, with a beauty that did not stay in the camera, it would get into the soul of whoever watched her. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut Movies Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics' Circle Inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award

"She had a way of being in the world that you don’t learn; you take in. People like Veruschka don’t go away at all. They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”

One of the first supermodels, Veruschka in the 1960s and ‘70s appeared often on covers of Vogue and other magazines around the globe. With a high forehead, blue-eyed gaze and sculptured, distinctive cheekbones, she stood more than six feet tall and was a muse for designers including Karl Lagerfeld , Yves Saint Laurent and Valentino .

“What made the German model so mesmerizing was her seeming disinterest in preserving any one iteration of that beauty,” Anna Cafolla wrote in Vogue . “She could be imperious or impish, feral or feline, androgynous or opulently feminine. She could contort her impossibly long limbs into unreal configurations, traversing fashion magazines and the wider public’s consciousness with ease in a way that had never been done before.”

Vogue offers a look at her “most striking beauty looks of all time” here . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Veruschka did her first shoot wearing nothing but body paint in 1966, and after she left modeling in 1975, she collaborated with German sculptor-painter Holger Trülzsch for a series of avant-garde self-portrait photographs in which her painted figure dissolved into forests or sides of buildings.

On the big screen, she appeared as a version of herself in Michelangelo Antonioni’s Blow-Up (1966) when she’s photographed by David Hemmings’ character in London in the Swinging ’60s, and she had a brief turn as a high-stakes poker player in Casino Royale (2006).

Vera Gottliebe Anna Gräfin von Lehndorff-Steinort was born on May 14, 1939, in Königsberg, East Prussia (now Kaliningrad, Russia).

She was 5 when her father, Count Heinrich von Lehndorff-Steinort, was executed in September 1944 for his involvement in a plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler two months earlier. Her mother, Gottliebe, was sent to a prison camp as she and her three sisters were forced to live in a Nazi children’s home.

After moving from Hamburg, Germany, she was an art student in Florence when she was discovered in 1959 by photographer Ugo Mulas; before long, she was a full-time model, working in Paris, New York and Munich. She reinvented herself with a new name and returned to New York, where she found a champion in Diana Vreeland, then editor-in-chief of Vogue .

“I dressed all in black,” she recalled, “and went to see all the top photographers, like Irving Penn, and said, ‘I am Veruschka who comes from the border between Russia, Germany and Poland. I’d like to see what you can do with my face.’” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She appeared on 13 covers of Vogue ’s American edition and on the covers of its Italian, French and British editions as well. Along the way, she was photographed by the likes of Avedon, Penn, Rubartelli, Peter Beard, Francesco Scavullo, Horst P. Horst and David Bailey and became one of the highest-paid, most in-demand models of her generation.

She graced the cover of Life magazine in 1967, and a year later, Rubartelli famously shot her in a lace-up safari jacket from Yves Saint Laurent for French Vogue .

In 1971, she was the subject of the Rubartelli-directed fantasy film Veruschka — Poetry of a Woman and appeared in West German magazine Stern with 27 other women under the cover line “Wir haben abgetrieben!” (“We’ve had abortions!”) to advocate for making abortions legal.

She returned to the runway for Chanel in 1994, for Giles Deacon’s spring show in London in 2011 and for an Acne Studios lookbook in 2017.

Her autobiography, Veruschka — Mein Leben , was published in 2011.

Her beauty, Avedon said, “demands something, and you must extend yourself to meet the challenge or know that a kind of splendor is lost to you forever.”

articles.title: Told You So: Bake Off’s Semifinal Had An Issue I Called From Day 1
articles.summary: The writing was on the wall for The Great British Baking Show.
articles.content:
I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription . While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats , I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a big impact on the semifinals episode.

Unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had issues with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show , so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The studio behind hits such as Jujutsu Kaisen, Attack on Titan and more has a new Shonen Jump anime coming our way next year, and has dropped a new look at it ahead of its next big update during Jump Festa 2027 later this December. Shueisha's annual event is set to reveal a whole bunch of updates about all of the new anime and manga projects they have in the works for the next year and beyond, and that means we're about to get many new releases confirmed too.

Studio MAPPA, the studio behind Jujutsu Kaisen , not only has that franchise to worry about during Jump Festa 2027 , but there's also a new anime on the way also from the pages of Shonen Jump as well as Beat & Motion is set to make its debut next year. The anime adaptation for Naoki Fujita’s manga has dropped some special new art for the series ahead of the big event as it teases a new update is coming soon.

The anime adaptation for Beat & Motion was first announced to be in the works earlier this Summer, and it's likely that we'll get an update on what to expect from it during Jump Festa 2027 . Taking place over the December 19-20 weekend in Japan, the annual event shows off many of the new anime and manga titles that are in the works. Shueisha often showcases quite a bit during this time, and it often comes with new visuals, trailers and even more for some releases. That would be the perfect time for a new update on this series too.

Beat & Motion will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix sometime in 2027 , but has yet to confirm any concrete release details as of this time. The new series will be directed by Yuki Komada for Studio MAPPA with Misaki Morie providing the scripts, Kazunori Aoki handling the character designs, Takahiro Ogawa overseeing as animation producer, and dugout providing the sound production. It's also set to star the main duo of Shuichiro Umeda as Tatsuhiko and Aya Gomazuru as Nico.

Naoki Fujita's Beat & Motion is a pretty special series within the Shonen Jump library. It might have ended with only less than 50 chapters under its belt , but it was setting out to tell a small story that was able to come to its complete end. The creator won Shueisha's "MILLION TAG" reality show competition where they were seeking to find the next big creator, and as a result the series got its official serialization and this new anime adaptation with Netflix for its prize.

It's a story of two artists who inspire one another to pursue their respective dreams. One is an illustrator inspired by an up and coming musician, and the other is that musician who wants the illustrator to draw up a new music video for their song. It's a series that's bound to strike a chord when it hits, so how are you feeling about Beat & Motion so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Annihilation Was ’00s Marvel’s Best Story and I’m Tired of Waiting for Marvel Studios to Adapt It
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Marvel Comics has become the most popular comic company, something that basically began when they started their new superhero universe in the 1960s. While DC was sometimes able to compete with them, for the most part Marvel was on top. With success after success under their belt, the company decided to branch out, leading to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has become the most popular comic company, something that basically began when they started their new superhero universe in the 1960s. While DC was sometimes able to compete with them, for the most part Marvel was on top. With success after success under their belt, the company decided to branch out, leading to the creation of the Marvel Cinematic Universe . Spider-Man, the X-Men, and the Fantastic Four's film rights were sold, so Marvel Studios only had access to the Avengers, their related characters, and the other portions of the Marvel Universe. The MCU hasn't been all about adapting books, but it has adapted some of the best stories in the company's history. However, one has been missing and it's about time it got an adaptation – Annihilation .

The MCU's first three Phases went in numerous directions, adapting various stories, with the overall story of the MCU being the battle against Thanos, who was out for the Infinity Stones. Since then, we've moved on to the Multiverse Saga, which is partly adapting Secret Wars . With Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars coming up, we're looking at what is (probably) going to be a new Phase. I think it's long past time Marvel looked at adapting Annihilation . It's the perfect epic for the MCU and could go a long way in making it as popular as it was before Avengers: Endgame .

2006 was a massive year for Marvel. Civil War was breaking the Marvel Universe , pitting hero against hero on Earth. For the first six years of the decade, Marvel was putting out some of the best books ever, but there was one part of the universe that was being woefully ignored and that was the cosmic side of the equation. The history of Cosmic Marvel is quite interesting; in the '60s, it was basically the baby of Lee and Kirby, the two of them setting up the basics like the Negative Zone, alien races like the Skrull, cosmic horrors like Galactus, and amazing heroes like Silver Surfer.

In the '70s, Cosmic Marvel was Adam Warlock and Captain Marvel battling the Magus, Thanos, and the High-Evolutionary, with writer/artist Jim Starlin orchestrating the best parts. Characters like the Guardians of the Galaxy, Moondragon, Gamora, Pip the Troll, Star-Lord, Rocket Raccoon, and more started to pop up. The '80s would see Cosmic Marvel fade when Starlin left the company, but when he returned in the beginning of the '90s, he would bring back his favorites and kick off the Infinity Trilogy, starting with Infinity Gauntlet.

'90s Cosmic Marvel was the Silver Surfer, Warlock and the Infinity Watch, and Thanos. However, the lackluster ending of the Infinity Trilogy would lead to Cosmic Marvel fading away again. That leads us up to 2006, when writer Keith Giffen, at the time also working on 52 , was part of a new Cosmic Marvel pitch, the one that would lead to Annihilation . The story saw something called the Annihilation Wave begin its runaway trip across the cosmos, destroying entire worlds.

In 2006, Cosmic Marvel was all but dead. The characters were all there, but no one had been using them. Giffen and writers Andy Lanning, Dan Abnett, Javier Grillo-Marxuach, and Simon Furman had their pick of characters and they started out with Silver Surfer, Nova, Super-Skrull, Ronan, and various living former Heralds of Galactus. It was a great mixture of characters, and fans ate the story up with a spoon. The Annihilation Wave was revealed to be under the control of the Fantastic Four villain Annihilus, the Kree betrayed everyone to team with him and survive, and even Galactus got involved in the war.

Annihilation was exactly the kind of big cosmic story that Cosmic Marvel did so well. I think one of the best ways to describe it is that it was old school and familiar, yet the story also felt fresh and new, partly because it was (Keith Giffen is one of our industry's greatest talents and he is dearly missed). Giffen and company were able to find the tone that made Cosmic Marvel work so well in the past – that sense of wonder and that anything could happen. The stakes were epic and fans loved it. It was a huge hit, helping Marvel further its lead in sales over DC, all while reintroducing classic characters. The story would birth numerous sequels and is responsible for the creation of the Guardians of the Galaxy that everyone knows and loves.

Marvel Studios has been doing better as of late, but the whole situation feels rather tenuous. If the next two Avengers movies can't stick the landing, it's not going to be great for the studio. However, I think that if the company wants something as close to a sure thing as possible, then Annihilation should be the direction they take the MCU. It has exactly the kind of big spectacle that the MCU does well and it's a more malleable story than most fans realize. Plus, Marvel already has all of the big pieces set up.

We have the Fantastic Four, who can open the Negative Zone. We have the Kree and the Skrull, whose conflict is key to the story. There's Galactus, Surfer, and the Guardians of the Galaxy. Down the road Thanos gets involved in the saga, which gives Marvel the chance to bring back its biggest villain. Annihilation would have to be changed in various ways to fit the MCU, but fans are used to that by now. There are lots of Marvel stories the MCU shouldn't adapt , but Annihilation isn't one of them.

The MCU was able to bring superheroes to the masses, trying to be as close to the comics as possible. It could have failed miserably, but Marvel Studios was able to pull it off. However, the last few years haven't been able to find the success that used to be commonplace for Marvel. There's still entertaining projects and massive hits, but it's just not the same. Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars are going to be hits (unless Doomsday is really bad; it's not probable, but it could happen), but Marvel needs a plan again.

Annihilation can give them that plan. Marvel looks like it's going to be focusing on the Fantastic Four and the X-Men in the future, but both of those franchises are great for cosmic adventures – an argument can be made that Fantastic Four (Vol. 1) and Uncanny X-Men (Vol. 1) were the epicenter of Cosmic Marvel after Starlin left in the '80s. Most importantly, Annihilation gives the MCU a direction, one that would hype fans up for all of the movies, not just the big ones. The MCU needs to expand and Annihilation can be the key to its future.

What do you think about Annihilation ? Do you want the MCU to adapt it or would you rather they go another direction after the Multiverse Saga? Sound off in the comments section below.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google CD Projekt Red has shared a new update this week on the development of its sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , and it sounds quite promising. Although The Witcher 4 is the main focus of CDPR right now , the studio hasn't shied away from the fact that it's working on a follow-up to Cyberpunk 2077 as well. And while we're likely still quite far away from seeing Cyberpunk 2 in action, the studio has now shared new information on where it's at in development.

Detailed in a new call with investors , CD Projekt Red VP Karolina Gnaś briefly touched on Cyberpunk 2 and how the project is going. Although Gnaś didn't say anything definitively about when the game would be shown off, she did say that CD Projekt Red is planning to staff up more heavily throughout 2027. The implication is that these new hires will be brought in to work specifically on Cyberpunk 2 , which suggests the game should enter production either next year or in 2028.

"[The team is] making good progress with Cyberpunk 2 , we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production," Gnaś said.

CD Projekt Red beginning full development on Cyberpunk 2 in 2028 would actually make a ton of sense, as this year is also the same one in which The Witcher 4 is planned to release . While The Witcher 4 will almost certainly continue to receive new content and updates after its arrival, much of CDPR will certainly begin shifting its focus to the studio's next major game, which will be that of Cyberpunk 2 .

Assuming that things play out in this manner, this would result in Cyberpunk 2 not actually releasing until well after 2030. Given the sheer scale that Cyberpunk 2 will certainly have, the game will almost certainly have to be in production for a period of three to five years. This puts it on track to not launch until the next generation of consoles becomes available.

Still, even if Cyberpunk 2 is this far down the road, CD Projekt Red could begin teasing it a bit sooner. The original Cyberpunk 2077 had its first teaser trailers emerge years before the game ever saw the light of day. While there's always the chance that CDPR might not want to go about things in this same way, it leaves the door open for Cyberpunk 2 being revealed in some capacity in the months or year to come.

Top Gear is set to return to the BBC with entrepreneur, chef and self-proclaimed car fanatic Gordon Ramsay as its host.

The U.K.'s beloved, long-running series has been off air since 2022 after co-host Andrew Flintoff was involved in an on-set car crash. He suffered serious facial and rib injuries when his open-top vehicle overturned on Top Gear 's test track.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A cool new horror thriller is set to make its anime debut with Netflix later this week, and has dropped its official opening theme sequence early to help celebrate its premiere. This series might be missing out on the horror holiday season, but thankfully it's helping to boost up the final stretch of the Fall 2026 anime schedule . Fool Night is a new anime adaptation of Kasumi Yasuda’s original manga, and it's going to be taken on with two of the biggest anime studios around.

Fool Night is a post-apocalyptic series set in a world where there is such a lack of oxygen , people end up planting seeds within their body to keep the little flow of it there is left. It's likely going to be a solid thriller to cap off the year with, and thankfully it won't be too much longer before we see it in action. Fool Night has released its creditless opening theme titled "Shake! spit out" as performed by Tempalay ahead of the anime's debut, and you can check it out below.

Fool Night will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix on November 26th, and will be running for 12 episodes. All of those episodes will be available to watch at the time of release, and the ending theme for the series titled "Iki" as performed by Nowlu. It's going to be a pretty big project too as it's a joint collaboration between two of the biggest anime studios, Sunrise (which has overseen franchises like Mobile Suit Gundam ) and Shaft (known for releases like Puella Magi Madoka Magica ).

Atsuyuki Yukawa is directing the new Fool Night anime for Sunrise and Shaft with Ryo Shimura serving as assistant director, Jin Tanaka handling the series composition, Robert Sato providing the character designs, and Tatsuya Kato composing the music. The voice cast for the anime includes Koki Uchiyama as Toshiro Kamiya, Minako Kotobuki as Yomiko Horai, Junya Enoki as Akira Yatsuka, Aya Endo as Saeko Kanaeno, Kiyomitsu Mizuuchi as Jin Hiragishi, Shion Wakayama as Sumi Matsuno, Hiroshi Tsuchida as Ken Hikasa, Nobuhiko Okamoto as Nishi, Sayaka Senbongi as Meg Okumura, and Yumiko Kobayashi as Ivy.

Fool Night will also be debuting with an English dub release when it makes its way to Netflix , and it's going to be spearheaded by the likes of Adam McArthur as Toshiro and Olivia Liang as Yomiko but the majority of the cast has yet to be confirmed as of this time. The series is a darker post-apocalyptic tale with an interesting take on the world as the anime introduces an idea known as "Transfloration," where those dying plant seeds in their bodies to produce more oxygen.

It's been a weaker year for horror anime in general despite some standout releases, but this could end up bridging the gap thanks to its science fiction appeal. With it debuting on Netflix this week, it won't be too much longer before we see what it has to offer. How are you feeling about the new Fool Night anime so far? Hallmark Media is gearing up for new expansion into podcasting — aiming to add another vector for connecting with its fanbase.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the company’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom Has Nothing to Do With Tony Stark, But Continues a Marvel Trend
articles.summary: It’s no understatement to say that the entire MCU rests on Robert Downey Jr.’s shoulders. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It’s no understatement to say that the entire MCU rests on Robert Downey Jr. ’s shoulders. No matter what behind-the-scenes talents like Jon Favreau and Kevin Feige could come up with, the franchise falls apart without the right star to win over audiences and keep them coming back. And without the success of Iron Man , the MCU would have been over before it even began. To that end, it’s easy to see why—after a lukewarm reception to much of the Multiverse Saga and the MCU’s first box office flop —Marvel Studios would bring Downey back as the titular threat at the center of Avengers: Doomsday .

Downey’s run as Tony Stark lasted over a decade and spanned major roles in nine MCU films, not including his uncredited cameo at the end of The Incredible Hulk . So while no one doubts the Oscar-winning star’s ability to transform himself into Victor von Doom, many fans have been confused about how, if at all, Downey’s Doom would connect to his version of Stark. Especially with the MCU introducing the concept of variants (who may or may not resemble each other), fans still don’t know what to make of Downey’s casting in Avengers: Doomsday . At this point, the most shocking turn of events would be if Doom and Stark aren’t connected at all.

As soon as Downey revealed himself as the MCU’s Doom at the 2024 San Diego Comic-Con, the internet exploded with a bizarre mix of excitement, disappointment, and stunned confusion. Some fans had hoped that someone like Downey’s Oppenheimer co-star Cillian Murphy or Mads Mikkelsen — who had previously played the villainous Kaecilius in Doctor Strange — would win the role. Others simply felt that bringing Downey back smacked of desperation, as the MCU tried to win over fans who gradually fell off after the Infinity Saga. And that sentiment has remained somewhat unchanged, as Marvel has been content to let fans wonder rather than clarifying Downey’s casting. Here’s the moment Downey’s Doom was revealed to the world:

Fans immediately leapt into speculation mode, assuming that Doctor Doom must be a Stark variant gone awry. Perhaps in his universe, the character’s life took a decidedly dark path, leading him to take the villain route instead of evolving into a hero. Surely, Downey’s casting sets up a moment wherein those closest to Stark see a maskless Doom, enhancing the emotional stakes. But Feige has confirmed Doom isn’t a Stark variant . If true, this leaves fans back to square one, as they mercilessly try to solve the casting puzzle before Avengers: Doomsday opens. However, there is one glaringly obvious answer no one seems to be talking about.

Everyone seems determined to make sense of Downey’s casting. But could the answer simply be because he’s a great actor? After all, Downey himself has said he was drawn to Doom because he wants to play the “best hero” and the “best villain.” Perhaps his penchant for complicated characters and his untapped ability to go dark simply led Marvel to double-cast Downey in two different roles throughout the MCU. While this is the highest-profile example of an actor playing two roles, it certainly isn’t unheard of. Chris Evans, Josh Brolin, Gemma Chan, Michael B. Jordan, Benedict Cumberbatch, Linda Cardellini, Oscar Isaac, and David Dastmalchian are just a few of the actors who have played more than one live-action Marvel role.

Granted, some of these actors’ roles exist in separate universes, or they created separate characters with the aid of motion-capture technology. But for fans who wanted Mikkelsen to return to the MCU, it’s a bit hypocritical to expect Downey’s Doom to automatically tie back to Stark. In fact, double-casting Downey allows Marvel to have him on hand to sell the film and elevate it with his performance. There’s no real need for his two characters to be connected, especially if he keeps the mask on for most or all of the film. Besides, years before Iron Man , Downey first met with Marvel to discuss another role: Doctor Doom . So maybe the MCU just circled back to this idea for Avengers: Doomsday .

Is there a chance Doctor Doom isn’t connected to Tony Stark in Avengers: Doomsday ? Sound off in the comments!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

articles.title: Full Survivor Series 2026 Predictions Including Thoughts On This Cody Rhodes And CM Punk Storyline
articles.summary: Wait, is Team USA going to lose here?
articles.content:
WWE moved away from Survivor Series’ traditional format of all multi-man matches in the mid 90s. I get where Vince McMahon and company were coming from. It’s harder to build when you have so many moving parts, and it was harder to get people to buy PPVs back in the day without world title matches. In an effort to get back to the spirit of Survivor Series, Triple H has used a men’s and women’s WarGames match the last few years to keep that 5 on 5 format, but the event doesn't have quite the same prestige it once did . This year, however, he also threw in an old school Survivor Series elimination match, and the build has been the best thing on WWE television in months.

Fortunately, there are some other exciting matches to look forward to, as well. The men’s War Games will feature the Bloodline against the 946, the latter of whom feel like they’re building some real momentum and are an actual threat to win. The women’s War Games match hasn’t had quite the same build, but it still features some top talent and should be a good showcase for younger talent as well. Throw in a pretty compelling Women’s World Championship match with Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch , and the card is really pretty solid.

With all due respect to Team Mexico and especially Penta who currently holds the Money In The Bank Briefcase, this match is lopsided on paper. Cody, CM Punk and Seth are three of the biggest stars in the entire company, and Rhdoes especially does not lose unless it’s in a very key spot or in service of building to something larger or very memorably at WrestleMania 39, both . This match, however, feels like it’s really building toward something larger. It feels like a Mega Powers explode situation.

I feel like the long-term goal here is to move us into a feud with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez. Rumors have swirled that Perez was originally slated to win Money In The Bank. She appeared in Morgan’s backstage segment with her this past Monday. Lynch has talked about how Judgment Day is holding her back. She’s clearly going to play a factor here in some way. It would be easy to say she’ll turn on Morgan and cost her the belt, but I don’t think that’s going to happen.

For the longest time, I was sure we were headed toward an Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair break-up, but curiously, WWE really hasn’t teased much friction between the two lately, not since Tatum Paxley's early main roster promotion. Without that dynamic, this really just feels like a run of the mill babyfaces vs heels match that we would get at a house show.

This is the moment where we find out how WWE really feels about 946 and Royce Keys. They’ve been the primary antagonists on the show for months and have been presented like really dangerous and unhinged monsters we should take seriously. If they lose here, it kind of feels like that’s the end. I mean I’m not saying they’re going to get released, but it feels like that’s the end of the audience taking them seriously. They’re the ones stepping up and trying to prove they’re main event players. If they lose in their first big PLE match trying to do that, then that tells the audience all they need to know.

One of the interesting consequences of Banijay ’s merger with All3Media is that Stephen Lambert, who runs The Traitors producer Studio Lambert , has been reunited with his early work.

Before Lambert, a former BBC documentary producer, founded Studio Lambert in 2008, he was Chief Creative Officer at RDF Media, where he produced series such as Wife Swap and Faking It.

As a result of the merger, which values the company at around $8B, that brings together Banijay’s 130 production companies (including RDF Media, which was folded into Remarkable Entertainment in 2024) with All3Media’s 40 shingles, Lambert and his team, which includes Chief Creative Officer Tim Harcourt and U.S. President Jack Burgess, can now dig through his own archives in search of IP to plunder and shows to remake. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Lambert told Deadline, “We're excited to be part of a very big group. We're excited about the fact that we have access to a pretty significant rights library, including a whole lot of shows that we did at RDF that we suddenly have access to.” Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

It will look to see whether there’s any new life for franchises such as Wife Swap , which was most recently turned into a Real Housewives vehicle, Faking It , the “modern-day Pygmalion” that ran for seven seasons in the UK and was adapted for TLC in the early noughties, Secret Millionaire , which was remade for both Fox and ABC between 2008 and 2012, and youth-skewing reality show Shipwrecked .

The trio are aware that they are “a bit of an anomaly” within the broader Banijay group.

“There hasn't been quite enough clarity about the fact that we're not in the country-specific setup. We’re not an American company working to the American system and we’re not a British company working to the British system,” said Lambert. “We’re a bit of an anomaly, but an anomaly that comes from the fact that we're both British and American, and also we're not fully owned by Banijay, so that makes quite a big difference as well.”

They’re happy to be part of a big group, but they’re aware that “we hang and fall on our ability to come up with ideas and to sell shows and make them very well.”

“It's a new outlook for [the parent company], and so far everyone's been very accommodating of our desire to keep working in the way that has been working for us,” added Burgess.

They work closely with Jane Turton, the former All3Media CEO who is now Banijay’s Deputy CEO.

Turton told Deadline, “Working with Stephen and Tim and the team at Studio Lambert is always exciting. The ideas, the shows, the success and, of course, the personalities are all big. Big bold ambitious ideas developed and produced to the very highest quality. It is a pleasure to be part of the Studio Lambert team and especially so now that we are part of the bigger Banijay Entertainment with its many production territories, deep IP catalogue and expertise in distribution, digital and live.”

Unlike many transatlantic companies, Studio Lambert does not geo-block its ideas with key staff being incentivized to work on projects regardless of whether they land in the U.S. or UK.

This was intentional to allow Studio Lambert entry into the “exclusive” club of producers that are trusted to make big shows. Lambert said that it started with The Circle , which was originally developed for Channel 4 in the UK before becoming a hit among younger viewers and being adapted for Netflix.

“Our effort has been on these big, high-budget shows, which we knew that buyers, both in Britain and America, wanted. In this highly competitive market, [buyers] all know that they need these big, noisy tentpole shows. But they also know that if they order an idea and the people who are pitching it haven't got the experience of making those very expensive shows, then it's not just going to be a flop, it's going to be their careers that are a flop for having ordered it. So, it does mean that they have to go with those people that have got the track record,” he added.

The Circle led to The Traitors, which led to Squid Game: The Challenge , which led to Fallout Shelter: The Experiment.

The company is currently in the middle of shooting The Circle for Hulu, which is streaming three episodes a week, hosted by Tinx and starring a mix of civilians and celebrities from Disney shows such as The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, Vanderpump Villa and Dancing with the Stars.

“It's exciting, and fast turn as well. We’re making it one day, cutting it and then it’s on air 48 hours later,” said Harcourt.

It was somewhat of a surprise that Hulu was able to land the rights, given that Netflix had premiered two seasons as recently as 2024. Burgess said that Hulu’s unscripted chief Rob Mills “jumped on the opportunity”. “There was a moment where he could he could do it, and they were instantly on board,” he said. “It was competitive as well,” added Harcourt. “There were other people that were that that were interested. It’s amazing that they’ve been able to do it.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Studio Lambert’s most buzzy show also features civilians and celebrities, albeit in separate versions.

It has produced four seasons of The Traitors featuring civilians for the BBC, as well as an upcoming fifth one in 2027, and two celebrity versions. In the U.S., The Traitors: New Blood , featuring civilians, just wrapped its first season and was renewed for a second season by NBC , as well as four seasons of the celebrity version for Peacock and a fifth one coming next year.

“A format is always best if it works with civilians because then you know it's like waterproof,” said Harcourt. "The BBC One audience was never going to accept a bunch of celebrities running around in green cloaks so there [had] to be civilians. Then it success we can do it with celebrities.”

“Conversely, in the U.S., having those tried and true reality stars who brought an audience was really helpful to us on Peacock. It was a platform that had Love Island , but didn't have a ton of inventory there, and so you're asking different questions of the audience, and it's worked really nicely going the other way,” added Burgess.

The Traitors has also been renewed for three further seasons, through season eight , by Peacock. “We've already interested our grandchildren. They want to know who's going to be making the show in 2053,” joked Lambert.

The trio paid tribute to Mike Cotton, who is the creative director of the franchise, and exec produces both the U.S. and UK series.

They also believe there’s plenty of road for the format. “It’s still quite early in its life cycle. I’m sure if 27 years ago we were told that this little show Big Brother, that felt innovative, was still on the air everyone would have scoffed. It’s quite surprising how long the shelf life of IP actually is,” said Harcourt.

In terms of big-budget competitions, the company is also passing go at Netflix with an adaptation of iconic board game Monopoly .

Studio Lambert beat out around 50 rivals in a bake-off to land the right to produce the show , which has a $2M prize. It will see 12 contestants competing on a life-sized Monopoly board.

“It's a big world. We've brought the board to life, and we've taken the heart of the game, but changed it for television. I think the changes are brilliant,” said Lambert. “It turns out that a board game that every family ends up squabbling over makes for a really exciting reality game because those emotions are definitely brought to life in this game. Luckily, the board was too big for anyone to flip over,” added Burgess.

Before it became one of the go-to producers for large-scale competition series, the feather in Studio Lambert’s cap was Undercover Boss. The show became a “great utility player” for CBS, which initially launched in behind the Super Bowl in 2010 and went on to air over 130 episodes. The Skydance-owned network revealed in September that it was bringing it back and, this time, with a host in Drew Carey.

“Good shows never die, they just rest,” said Lambert.

The first version of the show launched after the banking crisis and Lambert added that anxiety in the workplace and the American economy got CBS to the point where people would want to watch it again.

“This season has been really fun because you realize just how different people’s work lives are now,” added Burgess.

While the company prioritizes big-budget competitions, it has also struck a number of partnerships that allow it to play in different genres. These include launching Inner Drive Entertainment with Jon Barinholtz and Rob Belushi and bringing Vivian Choi and Jill Goslicky’s MindMeld Entertainment into the fold. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

MindMeld focuses on reality shows and docuseries with the pair having worked on Bravo’s Below Deck, while Inner Drive is game show focused.

Burgess said that these teams bring different skill sets. MindMeld, for instance, may be able to take advantage of all of the reality stars that come through the Traitors universe. “I’m really excited about the stuff [these companies] have coming through,” he added.

“It wasn't that we thought we would help them make big shows like ours. It was more that we thought, let's [have] our main creative effort concentrate on these big shows. But because we want to grow in all different ways, and we like working with great people, it's a way of having different kinds of shows away from the main sort of thrust of what we're doing and by having a relationship with them, we would hopefully help them get stuff away,” added Lambert.

The trio are confident that there are “tons of big opportunities in unscripted in the American market at the moment”.

“I think we’re sort of at the end of a cycle of a glut of dramas that started in the pandemic and I think buyers see value in unscripted and the young large audiences that they can they can deliver,” said Harcourt.

Every seven years or so, a new unscripted format emerges and becomes the lightning rod for others, which is exactly what The Traitors did. “What I hope that the takeaway from that will be is that something big and bold can still be a really big broad hit in unscripted. The focus for us isn’t what’s the next iteration of Traitors, it more what is the next big shape of a show that will be popular,” added Burgess.

articles.title: Marvel Boss Squashes Ghost Rider Rumor, But I Don't Believe Him
articles.summary: Kevin Feige is denying a massive rumor about Ghost Rider, but in spite of these most recent comments, it still feels like this one will turn out to be true. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Kevin Feige is denying a massive rumor about Ghost Rider , but in spite of these most recent comments, it still feels like this one will turn out to be true. Although attention is currently on Avengers: Doomsday —and even Avengers: Secret Wars after that—there is so much coming to the MCU in 2028 , one of the biggest projects of which is Ghost Rider . It was announced during the Marvel Studios panel during San Diego Comic Con 2026 that Ryan Gosling would finally be getting his wish and will be stepping into the titular role of Ghost Rider for the MCU, with Shawn Levy set to direct. This, interestingly, means a repeat of the director and star duo's time together on Star Wars: Starfighter , but it's seeming as though Ghost Rider is garnering even more excitement than that movie.

At present, though, there is still so much we don't know about the MCU's Ghost Rider plans, including the plot of the movie and what other characters (heroes, villains, and otherwise) might be making an appearance. While those details are likely to be kept under wraps for quite some time, the rumor mill has been hard at work, and one of the most prominent rumors about the movie thus far has been that it will feature Heated Rivalry's Connor Storrie as the primary villain. However, in a new interview with Entertainment Weekly , Feige is denying that this casting rumor is accurate. Check out his exact comments below.

Known for the steamy romance Heated Rivalry , some may have been surprised by the rumor that Storrie would be joining Ghost Rider as a villain, but this casting actually makes sense; he would undoubtedly be great in such a role. Yet, Feige is coming out and shutting it down. Speaking with Entertainment Weekly , Feige said, "That’s a rumor. Not a very creative rumor, either…What’s a popular show? Maybe they’re talking to Marvel! But I won’t say anything other than that and other than when there are great people around, it’d be fun to talk with them."

It's possible, of course, that Feige is telling the truth, although as far as denials go, this one isn't exactly the strongest or the most convincing. And, adding to that, Marvel executives and stars have been known to stretch the truth when it comes to rumors such as these. Just look at Chris Evans' years of insistence that he was retired from his role as Steve Rogers in the MCU only to be returning in a major way in Avengers: Doomsday (with the final trailer for Doomsday suggesting that he will be a central figure). For that reason, it feels very possible that Feige is not being entirely honest and Storrie will indeed be joining the MCU. As always, only time will tell.

Would you want to see Connor Storrie as an MCU villain? Let us know (and why) in the comments down below.

articles.summary: The next round of PlayStation Plus free games for December 2026 has now been revealed prior to their arrival next week. While this lineup hasn't necessarily been one of the best seen in 2026, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The next round of PlayStation Plus free games for December 2026 has now been revealed prior to their arrival next week. Throughout November, PS Plus subscribers have been able to grab Dead Island 2 , Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered , and Monster Train 2 . While this lineup hasn't necessarily been one of the best seen in 2026, it hasn't been looked upon negatively either, primarily because there are technically five free games included in this bundle. Now, as we approach the final month of 2026, PlayStation has announced what PS Plus users can expect in its last round of giveaways for the year.

Set to arrive next week on December 1st, the next wave of PlayStation Plus free games will include Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 , Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 , and Amnesia: The Bunker . Of this group, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 is considered the marquee title for December, as the remastered version of these iconic skateboarding games just launched back in 2025. Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 and Amnesia: The Bunker are then a little more dated by comparison, but they still provide some fantastic variety in terms of genre for the month.

Perhaps the best thing about this PS Plus lineup for December is that all three games will be available on PS4 in addition to PS5. While PlayStation has somewhat been straying away from giving out PS4 titles in recent months on PS Plus, all three games this month will be playable across both PS5 and PS4. In addition, these games on PS Plus will also be up for grabs a little bit longer than normal, as they'll stay available until January 4th, at which point they'll be replaced by the first slate of freebies for 2027.

Outside of these free games, it's already known that Ratchet & Clank will also be joining the PS Plus Classics catalog in December . PlayStation announced earlier this year that the original entry in the Ratchet & Clank franchise that debuted on PS2 would be joining PS Plus before the end of 2026. Since it still hasn't been added to the service, this means that it has to drop in December in order for PlayStation to make good on this promise. Unlike the free games for December, however, Ratchet & Clank will only be available to Premium members, as titles on the Classics tier of PS Plus are only up for grabs to anyone at this level of the service.

How do you feel about this incoming wave of PS Plus games for December 2026? And which game of the bunch are you most looking forward to downloading and playing? Be sure to let me know for yourself down in the comments section.

articles.title: "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut
articles.summary: It's only fitting that one of the industry's most brilliant comedic actors should take on theater's biggest diva in 'Oh, Mary!': "I had these weird thoughts. I was like, 'I'm going to forget to go to the theater.'"
articles.content:
If there's one piece of advice Lolly Adefope wants to pass on to the next Mary Todd Lincoln, it's from Broadway's Maya Rudolph: Wear the kneepads.

The British star has taken her undeniably brilliant comedy chops to the stage, making her West End debut in Oh, Mary! 's London transfer and joining a steadily growing — and deliciously mischievous — lineup of actors to take on the neglected wife of Abraham Lincoln at the Trafalgar Theatre (Catherine Tate, Mason Alexander Park, Jinkx Monsoon, as well as the show's playwright Cole Escola among them). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics' Circle Inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award Movies Damian Lewis Boards Short Film 'Odessa' as Executive Producer (Exclusive)

The 80-minute musical, chronicling the days before the U.S. president's assassination from the point of view of his alcoholic, cabaret-fanatic spouse, is a breathless romp with dance numbers, growling and some belt-out show tunes — all in a wig and corset.

It took Adefope a couple of performances to realize it wasn't do-or-die each night. "At first I was like, 'This has to be all of my energy in every single second of the show,'" she begins to The Hollywood Reporter . "If you're going to do one big show at Wembley Stadium, then yeah, you can let it all out. But it's just not sustainable for the body to be under extreme tension for an hour-and-a-half. In the beginning, I was just kind of doing it like a panic attack. And then after a while I was like, 'You can actually chill.'"

It tracks that Adefope performs Oh, Mary! 's absurdity with the precision of a surgeon. She's been described as the best part of everything she's in — and it's true. The South Londoner might be globally recognizable for roles in Hulu comedy Shrill or even the canceled-too-soon Franchise , but here in the U.K., she's a titan of the British comedy circuit and possesses the kind of make-it-look-easy talent that some performers spend their entire careers searching for. Never is that more on display than in the BBC 's Ghosts , where Adefope ascertained household-name status with her scene-stealing portrayal of Kitty, an adorable Georgian noblewoman who also happens to be dead. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I think it came naturally to me," says Adefope about character comedy and her early stand-up aspirations. "It was probably a good thing that I didn't really have people in my life who were doing stand-up. It was all just a very class clown vibe, listening to lots of Radio 4 comedy, watching [comedy duo] Mitchell and Webb and absorbing comedy on Nickelodeon and Disney Channel." It wasn't until late into her teens that Adefope thought she could make a living out of it. "I had an idea that I wanted to be a comic actor," she says, "but that felt like a made-up thing."

What does any young person with dreams of making a career out of cracking everyone else up do? Hit the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, of course. The must-stop for aspiring stand-ups and comedy performers has taken over the Scottish capital every August for 79 years, and served as a springboard for some of the most famous creatives in the business, such as Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Richard Gadd, Emma Thompson and Graham Norton. "It's this one month where you get to live with all your friends and see your friends' shows and when I was doing it, I was like, 'I wish this was what real life was like!'" remembers Adefope. "Sadly, it's not."

But it did land her an acting agent, and with that came one of her first paid gigs: Josh Widdicombe's 2014 sitcom Josh . "The character's name was Catherine or something. But in the beginning," says Adefope, "it was called, like, 'Annoying Girl at Party.' And I was like, 'Sign me up!'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The more she acted, the more Adefope believed she thrived in that space — particularly character work. It was on the game show Taskmaster and a slew of other now-non-existent British panel shows that her profile rose even higher. But it was a 2017 sitcom with Jim Howick, Loaded , that crucially got her acquainted with a member of theater collective Them There. "Jim called me and he was like, 'We're making this taster of this show. It's called Ghosts ,'" she recalls. "'Would you want to be in it?'"

Them There, comprised of Howick, Mathew Baynton, Simon Farnaby, Martha Howe-Douglas, Laurence Rickard and Ben Willbond, raised a generation with the still meme-spawning series Horrible Histories , a sketch show depicting caricatured versions of England's most prolific historical figures.

They had a new pitch for the British broadcaster — a quasi-flat-share comedy in which a couple inherits an enormous stately home filled with the ghosts of those who spent time and died there throughout the centuries. Among the apparitions are a lightning-zapped caveman, a Regency-era poet shot in a duel, a boy scout counselor from the '80s with an archery arrow through his neck, a victim of the Stuart era's witch hunts, and a disgraced Tory minister who died mid-sex and is now destined to spend eternity without trousers on.

Five seasons later, and Ghosts stands in pride of place in the U.K.'s comedy hall of fame. Its unprecedented success has made superstars out of its cast, hatched versions in the likes of the U.S., Germany, and France, and accrued a cool $11.2 million at the British box office with last month's release of a feature film Ghosts: The Possession of Button House , reuniting the beloved characters after the show's end in 2023. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Since Katy Wix's Mary ascended to a higher plane, or, as the ghosts say, got sucked off ("What can you do?" asks her former co-star with a faux pout), Adefope is the only performer who isn't also a member of the writing team. She remains one of the show's blindingly bright spots (of which there are many). "Kitty was pretty similar to how they first described her, but I think at first she was more stupid," laughs Adefope about the initial conversations around her giggling, pop music-loving poltergeist. "But to this day, I'm like, 'She's the smartest ghost!' I didn't want it to be too two-dimensional — not that they would have ever written anything two-dimensional — but I am obsessed with Tituss Burgess [in Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt ] and Jack McBrayer in 30 Rock ; [the idea] that there's something going on underneath the surface of this sweet character," she says.

Indeed, it's in Adefope's immediate understanding of the smartest possible decision — a sly eye roll, sudden scream, or childlike outburst — that makes her work as Kitty so impressive. "I think a big chunk of it is probably wanting to make the rest of the guys laugh," says the star about keeping the rest of us guessing with Kitty's mannerisms. "Part of it is probably having a background in doing live comedy — it's quite good training for that kind of show because there are loads of us, and you don't get hours to do a take. Sometimes you do just have to think: 'What is going to make people laugh? What's the unexpected thing?'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She couldn't have predicted the way the show would resonate with Brits. "It's a very rare experience to make something that you love making and that people also love watching, because it's sometimes one or the other," says Adefope. But there certainly wasn't any talk of a feature film after that fifth and final season wrapped up, or Adefope would have "really held onto that."

In the movie, the ghosts race to rescue a wandering spirit who's possessed the body of a young boy before the child loses his life forever. "The writers always wanted to make sure that it wasn't just a bonus, extra-long episode," she says about the direction they took. "[They wanted it to feel] like it warranted being on a big screen, and it's so nice having people watch and validate that. […] It does deserve to be longer and bigger."

She would admittedly do "100 sequels," but the group is facing some major continuity hurdles. "The ghosts aren't meant to age, and every year we all think we look older," she laughs. "We don't know how long we could do it for, but I don't think there are any plans to do a sequel. But there were no plans to make any more after the TV show, so who can trust what they say?"

Adefope is certainly well-acquainted with the false hope of a fickle entertainment business. The Franchise , HBO's satirical superhero comedy from Jon Brown, Sam Mendes and Armando Iannucci, got the axe after one season (though it did also earn Adefope a BAFTA TV Award nomination). She repeats THR 's question with a knowing smirk: "Was it chopped down in its prime? It's a great question. I was disappointed about The Franchise ," she begins. "I think it was so funny when the trailer came out for The Studio and it was so similar to the show we were making. And it's won the most Emmys of any comedy ever [now]," she says about the Seth Rogen-led Apple TV hit. "So did we stand a chance?" The question lingers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Another U.S.-based project, Aidy Bryant's three-season Shrill , would take Adefope to Portland every year for 12 weeks. "That definitely felt like, 'Whoa, this is actor lifestyle vibes,'" she says about playing Bryant's British best friend and flatmate, Fran. "I loved Shrill so much, it was a dream," she continues. "[But] because I'd done a show before that called Miracle Workers in Atlanta, there was a period of time [and] even now people say, 'Where are you living at the moment?' I'm like, 'I do actually live in London,' but after that I [thought], 'Maybe I should try and do some British work just so that people don't think I've left.'"

It might not get much more British than the West End, where Adefope has set up camp for the first time in Escola's Tony Award-winning show. Its transfer has denied the naysayers here in London, extending its run and consistently pulling enormous audiences, including to Adefope's slot, which wraps up Dec. 5.

She saw the Broadway version — "I was so giddy" — and immediately told Escola afterward that they should consider bringing it to London. It never occurred to Adefope that she could take on Mary Todd Lincoln herself. "I have never really known where to start in the theater world," she muses. "But Oh, Mary! is just so my humor and it felt like my comic sensibilities matched it quite well. I let the phone ring," she adds. "I didn't beg for the audition myself," a glimpse of Kitty emerges in those fluttering eyelashes, "because I was too shy." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It might not be a shock to hear that Adefope is an electrifying First Lady, imbuing her portrayal with the no-holds-barred cheekiness the character necessitates. As is the joy of Oh, Mary! , seeing her version is an entirely different experience compared to her predecessors'. Adefope's Mary is uniquely her own. "I feel so lucky to be able to put my spin on something and for it to feel like it fits really well," she says. "Sometimes you get a script for something and you're like, 'It doesn't quite match with how I see the character.' But this [was] an amazingly lucky fit that I felt I could inhabit it."

After agreeing to take on the role, the nerves followed soon after. "I had these weird thoughts," confesses Adefope. "I was like, 'I'm going to forget to go to the theater.' And they're going to be like, 'Where is she?'" But those jitters were swiftly reduced when she remembered it's already a beloved, award-winning show. (The only tough part now is a hard-to-please audience, "[or] if they're quiet when I'm doing my manic, physical comedy." It's a rarity, she assures us.)

Until December, Lolly Adefope has her kneepads on. "For the characters to get slightly further from myself is always fun," she tells THR about what comes after. "I mean, Mary Todd Lincoln is quite far from myself, even though now I feel like she is me. But I'm doing lots of writing, and seeing where that goes, and [I'm] open to whatever comes next." What that might entail is anyone's guess, but one thing is for certain: this Ghosts alum will stay a pro at lifting spirits.

Lionsgate's "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping" continues to power the domestic box office, earning a leading $15.98 million on Tuesday. articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Pierrot Black Clover is reaching the final stretch of its episodes for Season 2 this year, but the latest episode really took fans by surprise with a sudden confession of love. Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the adaptation of the Spade Kingdom Raid arc from Yuki Tabata's original manga, and each […]

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Black Clover is reaching the final stretch of its episodes for Season 2 this year, but the latest episode really took fans by surprise with a sudden confession of love. Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the adaptation of the Spade Kingdom Raid arc from Yuki Tabata's original manga, and each new episodes brings the fights against the Dark Triad one step closer to their end. And the latest episode explored the fallout of the fight against Megicula we had seen before .

Black Clover Season 2 recently wrapped up the fight with Megicula, and it came with some major developments for Noelle Silva during the midst of it. The fight saw her realizing that she really has romantic feelings for Asta for the first real time , but the newest episode threw even her for a loop as another relationship is developing instead between Lolopechka and Gaja thanks to his sudden confession of love.

Gaja's confession to Loropechika was cute!! Also the look on everyone's faces 😭 pic.twitter.com/Hue4rl92pi

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 8 explores the immediate fallout of the fight with Megicula. It had seemed like Gaja had fully sacrificed himself, but Mimosa Vermillion arrived just in time to heal his fatal injuries. With Lolopechka also being freed from the Supreme Devil's curse, it was the first reunion between the two since they were last seen in the anime five years ago. Gaja had been fighting to rescue Lolopechka after she had been kidnapped from the Heart Kingdom, and wasted no time with her reunion with her at last.

Gaja fully confessed his feelings of love to Lolopechka, and it seems like the two of them are going to happily move forward with their new relationship. With how many of these types of romantic connections that have been seen in Black Clover so far, it makes a great deal of difference to see that a relationship is actually moving forward. It's not just someone hiding their crush on someone else through wacky understandings, and hopefully it could inspire Noelle to move forward with her own crush.

Black Clover Season 2 has yet to confirm how many episodes it's going to be sticking around for, but it's been made even more apparent with the latest episodes that it's going to be wrapping up its run later this year. The season has already seen two members of the Dark Triad being defeated, and the next one is close at hand . There aren't many fights left in the arc to explore from this point, so fans should get ready for the climax hitting sooner rather than later.

Black Clover is also leading towards its adaptation of the final arc from Yuki Tabata's original manga sooner rather than later, but it's likely going to be in a future season yet to come. But that's all yet to be officially confirmed one way or the other, so it's best to catch up with Season 2 now streaming with Crunchyroll to see what could be coming on the way next.

Crunchyroll brought back the new season of this beloved series in August this year as part of the Summer 2026 anime lineup. As the largest streaming platform for anime fans across the globe, Crunchyroll is home to several acclaimed shows and movies, including Donghua, a term used for Chinese animation . The industry has been on the rise for the past few years, with Link Click being one of the most notable series thanks to its global availability on Crunchyroll. The donghua is based on an original story, and it centers around mind-bending mysteries while blending supernatural themes.

The story has always been kind of intense and heartbreaking, but things have taken a turn for the worse in the latest season. The first part of Season 3 reached its conclusion last weekend, and the anime confirmed the release window of Part 2 right away. Fans also got the first look at the second part and everything else we can expect from the story going forward. The official YouTube channel of Bilibili shared the second part's trailer while the official X handle dropped a new key visual.

Link Click Season 3 Part 2 has confirmed a 2027 release window, and the anime is expected to premiere in the second half of next year. However, the exact release date won't be announced anytime soon. Link Click doesn't always follow the quarterly schedule on Crunchyroll, where all anime series are released around the first two weeks of the month after TV broadcast in Japan.

While most of the Summer anime are released in July, Link Click released its third season a month later, and it's quite possible the anime will follow a similar schedule this time as well. Additionally, we can expect the anime to return on Crunchyroll, where you can also find all the episodes.

The trailer is more than enough to convince fans that the upcoming season will be more gruesome than ever, where Lu Guang will face a major threat to his life. The story doesn’t shy away from taking fans on an emotional rollercoaster with the dark themes and heart-wrenching tragedies, and the latest season has made it clear that things will only continue to get worse.

The key visual also highlights the true extent of the horrors that Xiaoshi and Guang will keep facing from here on out, as they stand in front of several corpses. Needless to say, the situation appears to be far worse than anything they both have ever faced so far. Additionally, we can also expect more plot twists in the upcoming episodes that will completely turn the lives of everyone in Time Studio upside down.
